en bugt.explanation: "En bugt" means "a bay". It has a second meaning, "a bend", as in a river. To say there is a bend in a river, use the same word: "en bugt i floden" (a bend in the river).

en bule.explanation: "En bule" means "a dent". It also means "a bump" on the body. To say you have a bump on your forehead, use the same word: "en bule i panden" (a bump on the forehead).

en bums.explanation: "En bums" means "a pimple". To say where a pimple is, add the place: "en bums i panden" (a pimple on the forehead).

en bund.explanation: "En bund" means "a bottom", as in the lowest part of something. To say something lies at the lowest point of the sea, say: "på bunden af havet" (on the bottom of the sea). The word is also in "en tærtebund" (a pie base).

en bundlinje.explanation: "En bundlinje" means "a bottom line". It is built from "bund" (bottom) and "en linje" (a line).

en bunke.explanation: "En bunke" means "a pile". To talk about a pile of clothes, say: "en bunke tøj" (a pile of clothes). To say someone has a large amount of money, use the same word: "en bunke penge" (a large amount of money).

en burger.explanation: "En burger" means "a burger". To name a burger without meat, put the main ingredient first: "en vegetarburger" (a vegetarian burger).

en bus.explanation: "En bus" means "a bus". To say you travel by bus, use "at tage" (to take): "Jeg tager bussen" (I take the bus).

en busbillet.explanation: "En busbillet" means "a bus ticket". It is built from "bus" (bus) and "en billet" (a ticket); "billet" is also in "en biografbillet" (a cinema ticket) and "en koncertbillet" (a concert ticket).

en buschauffør.explanation: "En buschauffør" means "a bus driver". It is built from "bus" (bus) and "en chauffør" (a driver); "chauffør" is also in "en taxachauffør" (a taxi driver) and "en lastbilchauffør" (a truck driver).

en busk.explanation: "En busk" means "a bush". To name a bush by the flower it carries, put the flower first: "en rosenbusk" (a rose bush).

en butik.explanation: "En butik" means "a shop". To name a shop by what it sells, put the goods first: "en blomsterbutik" (a flower shop).

en butiksansat.explanation: "En butiksansat" means "a store employee". It is built from "en butik" (a shop) and "ansat" (employed).

en butiksindehaver.explanation: "En butiksindehaver" means "a shop owner". It is built from "en butik" (a shop) and "en indehaver" (a holder). To say who holds a card, "indehaver" works on its own: "indehaveren af kortet" (the holder of the card).

en butikskæde.explanation: "En butikskæde" means "a store chain". It is built from "en butik" (a shop) and "en kæde" (a chain); "kæde" is also in "en hotelkæde" (a hotel chain) and "en cykelkæde" (a bicycle chain).

en butterfly.explanation: "En butterfly" means "a bow tie". To talk about the insect, use "en sommerfugl" (a butterfly): "En sommerfugl sidder på blomsten" (A butterfly is sitting on the flower).

en by.explanation: "En by" means "a town". The same word also means "a city". To call a big place a city, say: "København er en by" (Copenhagen is a city). To say you are in town, use "i byen": "Jeg er i byen" (I am in town).

en bydel.explanation: "En bydel" means "a district". It is built from "en by" (a town) and "en del" (a part); "del" is also in "en landsdel" (a region of a country) and "en verdensdel" (a continent).

en byfest.explanation: "En byfest" means "a town festival". It is built from "en by" (a town) and "en fest" (a party); "fest" is also in "en fødselsdagsfest" (a birthday party).

en byge.explanation: "En byge" means "a shower", as in a short spell of rain. For the shower you wash in, use "et brusebad": "Jeg tager et brusebad" (I take a shower).

en byggeplads.explanation: "En byggeplads" means "a construction site". It is built from "bygge" (build) and "en plads" (a place); "plads" is also in "en parkeringsplads" (a parking lot) and "en legeplads" (a playground).

en bygherre.explanation: "En bygherre" means "a developer", as in the person or company that orders a building. It is built from "bygge" (build) and "en herre" (a lord).

en byrde.explanation: "En byrde" means "a burden". To say someone is carrying a burden, use "at bære på" (to carry): "Han bærer på en stor byrde" (He is carrying a big burden).

en bytteseddel.explanation: "En bytteseddel" means "a gift receipt". It is built from "at bytte" (to swap) and "en seddel" (a slip); "seddel" is also in "en pengeseddel" (a banknote).

en båd.explanation: "En båd" means "a boat". To talk about a large ship, use "et skib" (a ship): "Skibet sejler til Norge" (The ship sails to Norway).
